questions.q: Match each financial term with its meaning.

pairs.r: A fixed amount paid every month to repay a loan
A regular payment made to an insurance company
A return that a shareholder may earn
An amount of money owed to somebody
The profit earned from an investment

questions.explanation: An EMI is the fixed monthly instalment that repays a loan; a premium is the regular payment to an insurance company; dividends are earned by shareholders; debt is money owed to somebody; and return is the profit earned from an investment.
questions.fact: An EMI (equated monthly instalment) is the fixed amount of money a person pays every month to repay a loan... Debt: Amount of money owed to somebody... Return is the profit earned from an investment.

questions.q: What is insurance?
options: A legal contract in which an individual pays a premium and the company compensates for covered losses
A savings scheme that doubles your money every year
A tax paid to the government on health expenses
A loan given by a bank to pay hospital bills
questions.explanation: Insurance is a legal contract: the individual pays a regular amount called the premium, and the insurance company agrees to provide financial compensation for specific losses or expenses covered under the policy.
questions.fact: Insurance is a legal contract in which an individual pays a regular amount, called a premium, to an insurance company. In return, the company agrees to provide financial compensation for specific losses or expenses covered under the policy.

questions.q: Insurance works on the principle of risk sharing, where many people pay premiums into a common pool.
questions.explanation: Insurance pools premiums from many people; when an unexpected loss occurs, those insured receive financial support from the insurance company. This is the principle of risk sharing.
questions.fact: Insurance works on the principle of risk sharing. Many people pay premiums into a common pool. In case of any unexpected loss, those insured receive financial support from the insurance company.

questions.q: A family pays ₹500 every month for health insurance, and a family member then needs medical treatment. What does the chapter say happens?
options: The family must pay the entire hospital bill from its savings
The insurance company covers a large part of the hospital expenses
The family's premium is returned and the policy is closed
The government pays the premium for that month
questions.explanation: In the chapter's example, if a family member requires medical treatment, the insurance company covers a large part of the hospital expenses—without insurance, the family might have to use a substantial portion of its savings.
questions.fact: If a family member requires medical treatment, the insurance company covers a large part of the hospital expenses.

questions.q: Select all correct statements about the benefits of insurance.
options: It provides financial security during emergencies
It helps families recover from financial setbacks
It encourages people to save and plan through regular premium payments
It guarantees profits on all your investments
questions.explanation: Insurance provides financial security during emergencies, reduces the impact of accidents, illness or property damage, helps families recover from setbacks, and encourages saving through regular premium payments. It does not guarantee investment profits.
questions.fact: Insurance provides financial security during emergencies, reduces the impact of accidents, illness, or property damage, helps families recover from financial setbacks, and encourages people to save and plan their finances through regular premium payments.

questions.q: Select all expenses that health insurance helps cover.
options: Hospitalisation
Medicines
Diagnostic tests
A new cricket bat
questions.explanation: Health insurance helps cover medical expenses such as hospitalisation, medicines, diagnostic tests, and treatments, reducing the financial burden of illness or accidents.
questions.fact: Health insurance helps cover medical expenses, such as hospitalisation, medicines, diagnostic tests, and treatments.

questions.q: Which government scheme provides health insurance coverage to eligible low-income households in India?
options: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
National Savings Certificate
BSE SENSEX
questions.explanation: In India, the government scheme Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana provides health insurance coverage to eligible low-income households.
questions.fact: In India, government schemes such as Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana provide health insurance coverage to eligible low-income households.

questions.q: Life insurance provides financial support to a family if the policyholder, who may be the breadwinner, passes away.
questions.explanation: Life insurance supports dependents if the breadwinner dies—it helps them meet daily expenses, continue children's education, and repay loans.
questions.fact: Life insurance provides financial support to a family if the policyholder, who may be the breadwinner of the family, passes away.

questions.q: Match each type of insurance with what it protects.

pairs.r: Covers medical expenses such as hospitalisation and medicines
Supports the family if the breadwinner passes away
Covers repair costs and damages from vehicle accidents
Protects homes and businesses against fire, theft, flood and earthquake
Protects farmers against loss from death or disability of animals

questions.explanation: Health insurance covers medical costs; life insurance protects dependents after the breadwinner's death; motor insurance covers vehicle accident damage; property insurance covers disasters like fire and theft; and cattle insurance covers farmers' animals.
questions.fact: Motor insurance covers repair costs and damages caused by vehicle accidents. Property insurance protects homes and businesses against losses caused by fire, theft, flood, earthquake, and other disasters. Cattle insurance protects farmers and dairy owners against financial loss in case of death or disability of their animals.

questions.q: Select all types of general insurance.
options: Motor insurance
Crop insurance
Life insurance
Health insurance
questions.explanation: General insurance protects against losses related to vehicles, homes, businesses and other property—motor, property, crop and cattle insurance are its types. Life and health insurance are listed as separate categories.
questions.fact: General insurance protects against losses related to vehicles, homes, businesses, and other property.

questions.q: Crop insurance protects farmers from financial losses caused by—
options: natural disasters, pests, and market price changes
their children's school fees
the purchase of household appliances
the premium paid on life insurance
questions.explanation: Crop insurance covers damages caused by natural disasters, pests, and market price changes, thereby protecting farmers from financial losses.
questions.fact: Crop insurance protects farmers from financial losses as it covers damages caused by natural disasters, pests, and market price changes.

questions.q: Which of these statements about insurance is INCORRECT?
options: Insurance companies collect the entire premium only once in a person's lifetime
Insurance is a legal contract between an individual and an insurance company
The regular amount paid for an insurance policy is called the premium
Without insurance, a family might use a substantial portion of its savings for treatment expenses
questions.explanation: The premium is a regular amount—paid every month in the chapter's ₹500 health insurance example—not a one-time lifetime payment.
questions.fact: Insurance is a legal contract in which an individual pays a regular amount, called a premium, to an insurance company.

questions.q: According to the chapter, which of these is a productive use of borrowing?
options: Taking an education loan to pursue higher education
Borrowing to buy unnecessary consumer goods
Borrowing to spend on impulse shopping
Taking a loan to gamble on share prices
questions.explanation: An education loan helps a student pursue higher education, which is a productive purpose, whereas borrowing for unnecessary consumer goods may lead to a debt burden and financial difficulties.
questions.fact: An education loan can help a student pursue higher education, whereas borrowing money to purchase unnecessary consumer goods may lead to a debt burden and financial difficulties.

questions.q: Responsible borrowing means taking loans only when necessary and ensuring that they can be repaid on time.
questions.explanation: The chapter defines responsible borrowing this way, so that credit remains helpful for productive purposes instead of becoming a burden.
questions.fact: Responsible borrowing involves taking loans only when necessary and ensuring that they can be repaid on time.

questions.q: EMI stands for ___.
questions.explanation: An EMI (equated monthly instalment) is the fixed amount of money a person pays every month to repay a loan.
questions.fact: An EMI (equated monthly instalment) is the fixed amount of money a person pays every month to repay a loan.

questions.q: A family buys a refrigerator costing ₹30,000 and repays the loan through an EMI of ₹3,000 every month for 12 months. What is the total amount repaid over the year?
questions.explanation: Twelve EMIs of ₹3,000 add up to ₹36,000. The extra ₹6,000 over the price is the interest, because each EMI includes a portion of the principal as well as the interest charged by the lender.
questions.fact: They may take a loan and repay it through an EMI of ₹3,000 every month for 12 months. Each EMI includes a portion of the original loan amount (the principal) as well as the interest charged by the lender.

questions.q: Which of these statements about EMIs is INCORRECT?
options: EMIs are commonly used to purchase mobile phones, household appliances, two-wheelers, homes, and cars
An EMI is a one-time payment made only at the end of a loan
Each EMI includes a portion of the principal as well as the interest charged by the lender
Paying through EMIs lets a family spread the cost of a purchase instead of paying the whole amount at once
questions.explanation: An EMI (equated monthly instalment) is a fixed amount paid every month, not once at the end—each instalment combines part of the principal with the lender's interest.
questions.fact: An EMI (equated monthly instalment) is the fixed amount of money a person pays every month to repay a loan.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Borrowing money to purchase unnecessary consumer goods may lead to a debt burden and financial difficulties.
Reason (R): Responsible borrowing involves taking loans only when necessary and ensuring that they can be repaid on time.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but R states the general rule of responsible borrowing; it does not explain why buying unnecessary consumer goods on credit creates a debt burden.
questions.fact: Borrowing or using credit can be helpful when it is used for productive purposes, but it can become harmful if misused.

questions.q: In personal finance, risk refers to the chance of ___ from an investment.
questions.explanation: Risk is the chance of losing money. Lower-risk investments like fixed deposits offer lower returns, while higher-risk investments may offer higher returns.
questions.fact: Risk refers to the chance of losing money.

questions.q: What does 'time horizon' mean when choosing an investment?
options: The length of time for which money can remain invested
The date on which a bond pays its first interest
The number of years a bank has operated
The time taken to open a fixed deposit
questions.explanation: Time horizon is the length of time for which money can remain invested. It is one of the four factors—along with risk, return and liquidity—to consider before investing.
questions.fact: Time horizon is the length of time for which money can remain invested.

questions.q: According to the chapter, what are taxes?
options: Compulsory payments made to the government to fund public services
Optional donations to insurance companies
Profits earned by shareholders in a company
Monthly instalments paid to repay a loan
questions.explanation: Taxes are compulsory payments made by individuals and businesses to the government to fund public services such as schools, hospitals, transport, and defence.
questions.fact: Taxes are compulsory payments made by individuals and businesses to the government to fund public services, such as schools, hospitals, transport, defence, and other essential facilities.

questions.q: Select all public services that taxes help fund.
options: Schools
Hospitals
Defence
Pocket money for children
questions.explanation: Tax money funds public services such as schools, hospitals, transport, defence, and other essential facilities—not private payments like pocket money.
questions.fact: Taxes are compulsory payments... to fund public services, such as schools, hospitals, transport, defence, and other essential facilities.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an indirect tax?
options: Income tax
Goods and Services Tax (GST)
Tax on business profits
Tax on a person's salary
questions.explanation: Indirect taxes are added to the price of goods and services, and the GST is the chapter's example. Income tax, by contrast, is a direct tax paid on income or profits.
questions.fact: Indirect taxes, which are added to the price of goods and services, such as the Goods and Services Tax (GST).

questions.q: Indirect taxes are paid directly on a person's or organisation's income or profits.
questions.explanation: That describes direct taxes, such as income tax. Indirect taxes are instead added to the price of goods and services, like the GST.
questions.fact: Direct taxes, which are paid directly on a person's or organisation's income or profits, such as the income tax.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Insurance helps reduce the financial impact of accidents, illness, or property damage.
Reason (R): Many people pay premiums into a common pool, and those who face unexpected losses receive financial support from it.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Both A and R are true, and R explains A: because premiums are pooled, an individual's loss is shared among many insured people, so the financial impact on any one family is greatly reduced.
questions.fact: Insurance works on the principle of risk sharing. Many people pay premiums into a common pool. In case of any unexpected loss, those insured receive financial support from the insurance company.
